newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks to set up Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks to set up Holocaust fund.

text.p: Switzerland's three biggest banks, bowing to international pressure, said on Wednesday that they had agreed to establish a 100 million Swiss franc ($70.1 million) Holocaust memorial account.

"Reflecting the intensive discussions which are under way in Switzerland to create such a fund, the banks said the time has come for action, not words," they said in a joint statement. ($ = 1.426 Swiss Francs)

The banks -- Union Bank of Switzerland, Swiss Bank Corp and Credit Suisse Group -- said the special escrow account would be the basis for the "Humanitarian Fund for the Victims of the Holocaust" and was open for more contributions from others, including the Swiss government and the central bank.
The statement also stressed that in the banks' view, efforts underway to identify unclaimed assets belonging to victims of the Nazi regime are separate from and unaffected by this initiative.

They also stated that this move would clear the way for the Swiss government, the Swiss business and financial community and Jewish organisations to work together towards finding a just and equitable solution to the issues involved.
The funds have been deposited with Switzerland's central bank for the time being until the Swiss government determines how the fund will be structured, the statement also said.
